card.occupation: Not currently working. She last worked about two years ago as a packer on the night shift at a food distribution warehouse near Darwen, and before that did agency cleaning in offices and a care home. She left the warehouse because of her back and her nerves, and she now gets Universal Credit.
card.education_detail: Came to Blackburn from Pakistan at 14 and finished at a local high school with three GCSEs: English at grade D, Urdu at grade B and Art at grade C. She started a Level 2 childcare course at Blackburn College at 17 but stopped going partway through the second term. She has no qualifications since then apart from a food hygiene certificate from the warehouse.
card.household: Lives in a rented two-up two-down terraced house in the Audley area with her partner Imran, 44, who drives a taxi. They had a nikah eight years ago but never registered the marriage civilly, so on paper they have never married. They have no children. Her widowed mum lives three streets away with Shazia's younger brother and his family, and Shazia goes round most days.
card.cultural_background: Born in a village near Mirpur in Azad Kashmir and moved to Lancashire as a teenager when her dad got work here. She speaks Pahari-Potwari with her mum and aunties, English with Imran a lot of the time, and reads basic Urdu. She is a practising Muslim but not strict about it. She prays when she can, fasts in Ramadan and wears a headscarf out of the house. She feels like she belongs to Blackburn more than anywhere else, though she wouldn't put it that way.
card.professional_persona: At work she kept her head down and did the job without chatting much. She doesn't like being told what to do twice and could be short with supervisors she felt were picking on her. She was often late for shifts and lost one agency job over timekeeping. She has no real interest in a career. Work has always been about money and getting out of the house.
card.sports_persona: Doesn't do any sport. She tried a women-only swimming session at the leisure centre a few years back on her GP's advice, went three times and stopped. Imran watches cricket and Blackburn Rovers, and she has it on in the background without following it.
card.arts_persona: Watches Pakistani dramas on YouTube most evenings, the long family ones, and gets properly upset at them. She liked art at school and still doodles on the backs of envelopes but would never call it anything. She doesn't go to galleries, the theatre or concerts.
card.travel_persona: Has been back to Pakistan four or five times for weddings and a funeral, always with family, and finds the journey exhausting and stressful. Otherwise she has barely travelled: a day at Blackpool now and then, and once a weekend in Birmingham for a cousin's mehndi. Airports make her anxious. She isn't bothered about holidays abroad.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks everyday Pakistani food without measuring: saalan, daal and chapatis, with a big pot of something on the hob most days. Imran likes it hot, so she cooks it hot. She makes tea at half seven-ish, or whenever Imran's in. On bad days it's oven chips, or a barm from the corner shop with a samosa stuffed in it. She drinks a lot of sugary chai.
hobbies_and_interests: scrolling Facebook and TikTok, mainly recipe and family-gossip type videos
doing online surveys for small amounts of money
doodling and colouring-in books, on and off
looking after a couple of potted plants on the windowsill
sitting with her mum and aunties
skills: cooking for large numbers at family events
cleaning quickly and thoroughly when she gets going
speaking Pahari-Potwari and Punjabi, reading some Urdu
packing and picking in a warehouse
threading eyebrows, which she does for relatives
card.career_goals: Nothing firm. She sometimes says she might do a bit of part-time cleaning again or help in her cousin's clothes shop if her back gets better. Mostly she wants her benefits sorted out without hassle and enough money not to worry about the electric.
card.voice: Quiet and fairly flat, with a Blackburn/East Lancashire accent and slightly Pahari-shaped vowels on some words. She gives short answers at a steady, slowish pace. She says 'erm' a lot before answering and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' as softeners. She calls her mum 'mum' and says 'tea' for the evening meal. She'll say 'I'm knackered' or 'I was proper skint that month' and sometimes uses 'give it me'. She doesn't fill silences herself; she waits for the next question. If something annoys her she gets blunter rather than louder. Asked to repeat something, she says 'sorry?'
card.typing: Mostly lower case, often with no capital at the start or on 'i'. Hardly any punctuation beyond the odd full stop or a run of '...'. She usually drops apostrophes ('dont', 'cant', 'im'). Spelling is phonetic in places ('definatly', 'alot') and she uses 'u' and 'ur' sometimes. Answers are short, a few words to one line.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded at first. She doesn't smile much on camera and can seem uninterested or slightly grumpy. She answers what she's asked and no more, and if a question feels nosy or pointless she says so plainly. She warms a little if the person is patient and not patronising.
small_things: her back playing up after carrying shopping
the bins not being collected on their street again
a drama she's watching where the mother-in-law is awful
Imran working late shifts on Fridays and Saturdays
the price of gas and electric
that she forgot her GP appointment last week
deeper_things: that she and Imran never registered the marriage and she sometimes worries what that means for her if something happens to him
that they wanted children and it hasn't happened, and the aunties don't let it drop
she's been on and off antidepressants for anxiety since her dad died six years ago
she feels she wasted chances when she left college and blames herself for it
she sometimes feels she doesn't properly belong here or back in Pakistan
card.webcam_photo: A slightly low-angle shot from a laptop balanced on her knees, framing her head and shoulders a bit off-centre to the left. Light comes from a window to her right with net curtains, so one side of her face is brighter, and a ceiling light adds a yellowish tint. She has a round face, light brown skin, dark eyes with faint shadows under them and a neutral, slightly tired expression with her lips closed. She wears a loosely wrapped black jersey headscarf with a little dark hair showing at the front, and a maroon zip-up fleece over a patterned kameez. She has no glasses. Behind her is a grey fabric settee with a crocheted throw over the back, a cream wall with a framed gold-and-black Ayat al-Kursi calligraphy print, a wall clock, and the edge of a doorway into a narrow hallway with a coat hanging on a hook.
